messages:
Maya (Support): Hey team, customer reports tool call failures when calling our invoice_fetcher tool via function-calling. They send a payload that includes a Windows file path and we get a 400 from the tool: \"tool args validation failed: invalid JSON\". Repro attached below.

Maya (Support): Repro steps: 1) Create chat completion with function name 'invoice_fetcher' and args stringified in the assistant reply. 2) Customer includes path like C:\\invoices\\2025\\Q1\\invoice_123.pdf inside a raw JSON string. 3) API responds with error and tool never invoked.

Maya (Support): Their raw assistant->tool args (copied):
```
{"customer_id": "acme-42",
 "path": "C:\\invoices\\2025\\Q1\\invoice_123.pdf",
}
```

Maya (Support): Note trailing comma + backslashes + they said they paste the object into a rich-text editor first.

Jamie (Support): Can reproduce locally with the same string. If I remove trailing comma it passes validation. Backslashes look fine when escaped but the combination + editor might add invisible characters.

Eli (Eng-ML): Thanks for the clear repro. Error likely from our JSON parsing step in the tool-router where we call json.loads on the tool_args string. That will fail on trailing commas. Two things to check: 1) content-type header the customer sends (should be application/json) and 2) whether our assistant reply wraps tool args in a raw string (we expect strict JSON).

Eli (Eng-ML): Quick patch suggestion: we can try a tolerant pre-parse that strips obvious trailing commas and unescapes Windows paths, then re-validate against the tool schema. But careful: we don't want to silently accept malformed args for security reasons.

Sam (SRE): Adding logs from runtime:
```
[2024-08-20T14:05:12Z] request_id=req_92b tool_router: parsing tool args payload: '{"customer_id": "acme-42", "path": "C:\\invoices\\2025\\Q1\\invoice_123.pdf",}'
[2024-08-20T14:05:12Z] request_id=req_92b tool_router: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 2 column 62 (char 73)
```

Sam (SRE): We don't currently emit a user-friendly error describing trailing comma vs general JSON error. Customer sees a 400 with \"invalid JSON\" and no hint.

Maya (Support): Customer is blocked because they pipe generated paths from a legacy system that outputs single-escaped backslashes and sometimes an extra trailing comma when building objects. They asked for a workaround we can recommend ASAP.

Jamie (Support): Short-term: ask them to run a quick sanitize step: replace "\\\\" with "\\\\\\\\" (i.e., double-escape backslashes) and remove trailing commas. Provide a one-liner python snippet: 
```python
import re, json
s = raw_string_from_client
s = re.sub(r",\s*}\n$", "}\n", s)
s = s.replace('\\\\', '\\\\\\')
obj = json.loads(s)
print(json.dumps(obj))
```

Eli (Eng-ML): Longer term: I'll add a defensive pre-parser in the tool-router that does two optional passes: 1) attempt strict json.loads, 2) if that fails, run a non-destructive sanitizer that (a) strips trailing commas from objects/arrays, (b) normalize common escape sequences, and (c) check for control chars. We gate this behind a config flag per-customer and emit detailed logs so support can see what was corrected.

Eli (Eng-ML): Risks: automatic corrections could mask faulty client behavior and may cause different semantics (e.g., accidental extra keys). So we'll only allow it for a short-term opt-in setting while we educate customers.

Maya (Support): That sounds reasonable. Customer wants an ETA and a documented workaround. Can we ship the opt-in sanitizer in staging this week?

Eli (Eng-ML): I'll open a quick MR with the sanitizer and tests today. If reviews go well we can deploy to staging within 48 hours. I'll include a detailed log message format: \"toolargs_sanitizer: applied_trailing_comma_fix=true applied_path_escape_fix=true\" so support can audit.

deploy-bot: Started deployment of branch/eng/sanitize-toolargs to staging (deploy-4567).

Sam (SRE): Watch that deployment for increased CPU on the tool-router instance due to extra parse attempts. Added an alert to track p95 parsing latency > 300ms.

Maya (Support): I'll send the temporary python snippet and instructions to the customer, and offer to flip the opt-in flag for them once the staging deploy is verified.

Jamie (Support): Customer confirmed they can sanitize on their side for now. They asked if our API could accept raw strings and expose a parse endpoint instead of failing the whole request. Could we add a 'tool-args/parse' endpoint?

Eli (Eng-ML): Good idea. I'll sketch a small parse-only route that returns a normalized JSON or an error with a helpful diff. Low risk and useful for customers integrating legacy systems. I'll include it in the MR.

Maya (Support): Thanks all — updating customer. Will follow up after staging deploy. :thumbsup:
